text:
maya: Pushing a compact welcome canvas prototype to the preview link — goal: faster first-run flow, fewer clicks to an API key + sample project. Can people scan for UX regressions and accessibility nits? :eyes:

sam: Looked at it. I like the smaller hero. Concern: the sample-project cards feel visually similar to the promo slots. Need clearer affordance that these are runnable templates, not marketing. Maybe add a small play/run icon and a disabled state when not authed.

jin: Agree about the affordance. Also the CTA order is weird — 'Create API key' sits to the left of 'Try sample project'. For keyboard users the focus order should follow task priority: create key -> run sample. I'll swap DOM order in the preview branch.

nora: Copy note: the top line currently says "Get started with Redwood" — suggestion: "Launch your first model in minutes" — more outcome-focused. Also add microcopy under sample projects: "Includes example prompts and runtime config" so people know what's inside before they click.

oliver: A11y quick pass: contrast on the secondary CTA (outline) is 3.8:1 on staging — below WCAG AA for large text. Also the card hover only changes background color; no visible focus ring for keyboard. Recommend explicit focus outline and ensure interactive elements have aria-labels. Example snippet: `button.run-project[aria-label="Run sample project: todo-app"]` plus `:focus { outline: 3px solid #0a66ff; outline-offset: 2px; }`.

sam: Nice. On dismissed banners — currently the welcome banner is dismissible but it reappears after a refresh if you haven't created a project. We should persist dismiss state per-user in local storage and also respect server-side flag for new signups. Don't want it nagging.

maya: Good call. Team: prioritize non-annoying behavior. I think we keep it dismissible until they complete either create-key or run-sample, then hide permanently. Also track telemetry for which option they choose. Add consent microcopy?

nora: Yes, add a short note under the banner: "We collect anonymized product events to improve onboarding — manage in Settings" with a link. Keep it subtle. If legal wants explicit opt-in later we'll re-evaluate.

jin: Quick frontend note: the compact canvas reduces layout height by ~120px which helps for small screens, but on <640px the sample cards wrap awkwardly. I'll add a breakpoint that stacks card content and hides the long description behind a chevron expand.

oliver: For screen readers, please ensure the card expand is `button[aria-expanded]` and announcements include sample project name + short summary. Eg: "Todo app — starter sample that demonstrates text generation and embeddings".

maya: Nice detailed calls — thanks. Can we A/B test two variants: A) compact canvas with inline sample cards (current preview) vs B) compact canvas + a single prominent sample with a "See more templates" link? Hypothesis: fewer choices -> higher run-rate.

sam: Yep. I'll wire analytics events: `onboard.sample_shown`, `onboard.sample_run`, `onboard.create_key_click`. Keep event payload small: user_id, variant, project_id.

deploy-bot: Preview deployed -> https://preview.redwood-inference/internal/welcome-canvas/1898765432 (build 2026.03.23-77).

jin: I'll push the keyboard/focus fixes and breakpoint changes to branch `welcome/compact-fixes` by EOD.

oliver: I'll run axe quick-check after those changes and post results.

maya: Action items: sam -> analytics + A/B flags; jin -> accessibility + breakpoint fixes; nora -> copy microtext + telemetry link; oliver -> verification. We'll reconvene tomorrow after the A/B wiring. :thumbsup:
